title: Finitary images of IID processes
exact_target: Must a Bernoulli measure of maximal entropy on a shift of finite type be a finitary factor of an IID process?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $X\subseteq A^{\mathbb Z^d}$, with finite alphabet $A$, be a shift of
finite type: it consists of the configurations avoiding a fixed finite
list of forbidden patterns and their translates. Suppose it has a unique
shift-invariant probability measure $\mu$ of maximal entropy, meaning
$h_\mu(\sigma)=h_{\rm top}(X)$. Assume also that this measure-preserving
lattice action is Bernoulli, that is, measurably isomorphic to an
independent product process.

Does there exist an independent identically distributed process
$Y\in B^{\mathbb Z^d}$ and a measurable shift-equivariant map
$\Phi:B^{\mathbb Z^d}\to X$ such that $\Phi_*\mathbb P=\mu$ and
$\Phi$ is finitary? Here finitary means that almost surely there is a
finite random radius $R(Y)$ such that the output symbol at the origin
is determined by the input coordinates in $[-R,R]^d\cap\mathbb Z^d$.
The same local rule, translated, determines every other output coordinate.

The input alphabet and its probability law may be chosen to suit $X$.
No tail estimate or finite expectation for $R$ is required. The map is
only required to be a factor onto the probability law $\mu$, not a
finitary isomorphism with a finitary inverse. Bernoullicity already gives
a measurable coding; the question is whether one can arrange that every
individual output coordinate is decided by a finite, configuration-dependent
window. A single deterministic uniform coding radius is not requested.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Must a Bernoulli measure of maximal entropy on a shift of finite type be a finitary factor of an IID process?
